reports.title: UK Electricity Mix Weekly Report: Thursday 27 August
reports.intro: A measured weekly report for EnergyMix.info using the available 7-day historical generation feed for Friday 21 August to Wednesday 26 August.
reports.summary: The week from Friday 21 August to Wednesday 26 August averaged about 22.8 GW of measured generation, with renewables averaging 44.5% of measured output. The strongest renewable day in the available data was Tuesday 25 August, when wind, solar and hydro together averaged 52.9% of measured generation. Gas was highest on Friday 21 August and lowest on Saturday 22 August.
reports.takeaway: For flexible electricity use, the cleanest opportunities are likely to appear when wind is strong, gas is low and demand is not at a peak. This is the foundation for future EV-charging guidance, clean-electricity alerts and weekly newsletter summaries.
drivers: Renewables were strongest on Tuesday 25 August, when wind, solar and hydro averaged 52.9% of measured generation.
Wind was the largest swing factor in the available feed, peaking at about 9.5 GW average output on Tuesday 25 August.
Solar was strongest on Sunday 23 August, averaging about 4.4 GW across settlement periods after embedded-solar backfill where needed.
Gas averaged about 4.5 GW across the period, rising highest on Friday 21 August and falling lowest on Saturday 22 August.
Measured generation was highest on Wednesday 26 August, at roughly 25.8 GW average output.

cleanestPeriods.title: Best low-carbon proxy: Tuesday 25 August
cleanestPeriods.body: Historical carbon-intensity aggregates are not yet part of this weekly report feed, so EnergyMix.info uses renewable share and gas output as cautious proxies. Tuesday 25 August had the strongest renewable share at 52.9%.

cleanestPeriods.title: Lowest gas proxy: Saturday 22 August
cleanestPeriods.body: Gas generation averaged about 2.6 GW on Saturday 22 August. Lower gas periods are often cleaner, but the report does not yet claim this was the lowest-carbon period without historical carbon-intensity validation.

higherCarbonPeriods.title: Highest gas proxy: Friday 21 August
higherCarbonPeriods.body: Gas averaged about 7.2 GW on Friday 21 August. Gas-heavy periods are usually higher-carbon, but this is labelled as a proxy until historical carbon-intensity highs/lows are added to the report feed.

socialPosts.title: Monday weekly grid brief
socialPosts.body:
Last week in Britain’s electricity mix:

• Highest renewable share in the available feed: 52.9% on Tuesday 25 August
• Highest average wind output: ~9.5 GW on Tuesday 25 August
• Highest average solar output: ~4.4 GW on Sunday 23 August
• Highest average gas output: ~7.2 GW on Friday 21 August

The shift was clear: gas-heavy weekdays gave way to a cleaner, wind-led weekend.

Full report: https://energymix.info/reports/weekly/2026-08-27/

socialPosts.title: Wednesday explainer
socialPosts.body:
What does “UK electricity mix” actually mean?

For live grid dashboards, it usually means Great Britain’s electricity system: England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the UK, but operates in a separate electricity market.

Explainer: https://energymix.info/uk-electricity-mix

socialPosts.title: Friday practical clean-electricity post
socialPosts.body:
The cleanest time to use electricity is not a fixed hour.

It changes with wind, solar, demand, imports and gas generation. Windy overnight periods and sunny middays can be much cleaner than still early-evening peaks.

Guide: https://energymix.info/cleanest-time-to-use-electricity
